Considerations of size of particles is very misleading. Because of the magnitude of the dust impacting the receptor and its immediacy to the source, many small particles may have been compressed and merged into larger particles. There is no consideration or measurement of the effects of control on size of particles that escape. It is stated that 90 percent of all particles will settle to the ground and not go into the air but there is no justification or explanation of this assertion. Is it based on the (potentially fallacious) assumption that the 90 percent of all particles reportedly greater in size than 10 microns and that they will soon settle out?
Several other air-quality-related points are not dealt with in sufficient detail. There is no discussion as to whether or not adequate water would be available for particulate control when there is fire fighting in the immediate vicinity and what the response would be if inadequate water were available. Similiarly, although the words control and precautions are used with reference to demolition of buildings containing friable asbestos, controls are never specified nor is it indicated how asbestos will be identified or demolition activities monitored to ensure application of controls/precautions.
The above problems must be addressed and rectified. In order to avoid repeated rounds of criticism, it would be appropriate for the consultants to identify assumptions, marshall their calculations and determine methodology for additional activities and discuss all these with personnel of the Division of Air Quality Control (contact person - Mr. Kenneth Hagg at 727-2658) prior to carrying out work or writing the final statement.
of particular importance is the need for additional monitoring which measures the ambient effect in the vicinity (as opposed to the immediate on-site dust production) of airborne dust and particulates which have not settled out. In carrying out this monitoring, consultants should place their equipment in such locations to be able to determine actual ambient effect of the project, including appropriate measurements to discount background particulate level. These measurements should be made for both controlled and uncontrolled demolition for both types of buildings. Data gathered should be appropriate for and used in simple dispersion modeling so as to better ascertain real effect and extent of demolition on both primary and secondary 24-hour standards and on annual averages. Consultants hould bear in mind that particulates affecting standards can be greater than 10 microns, but if there is particular concern as to size and distribution, sizing headers on monitoring equipment can be employed.
Water Quality: Consultants should specify the reasons for and calculations behind the statement that harbor siltation will not be increased beyond normal rainstorms as a result of run-off from demolition sites in light of the large quantity of settled out dust, and soil disturbance and compaction from heavy equipment operation.
